reconcile.connective: Gill reads Acts 9:8's "no man" as Paul's post-vision blindness, distinct from the Christ he says he had already seen.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses the plain conflict between Paul's claim to have seen Jesus and Luke's statement that he "saw no man."

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible (1999), contra/paul_see.html

excerpts.excerpt_text: …and when his eyes were opened he saw no man; neither Christ, who appeared to him from heaven, whom he had before seen, nor even any of his companions, nor indeed any object …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill glosses Acts 9:8's 'saw no man' as covering Christ too, but explicitly notes Paul 'had before seen' him — directly reconciling the verse with Paul's own claim in 1 Cor 9:1/15:8 to have seen Jesus.

pd_work.resource: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832), on Acts 9:7
pd_work.author: Adam Clarke
pd_work.note: Clarke poses the question directly — 'whether Jesus Christ did really appear to Saul on this occasion' — and resolves it by appeal to Paul's own words in 1 Cor 9:1 and 15:8, which he says 'put the subject out of dispute.'

link.title: CARM: Did Paul actually see Jesus?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment affirming Paul's post-ascension encounter with the risen Christ on the Damascus road as a genuine sighting.
